themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no stable number to grade your work against, and the thing being measured often moves while you measure it, so the models start by building a small truth set of their own or admit the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: On answer engine optimization all three models say the answers are personalized and non-deterministic with no fixed baseline, and the same gap shows up in cross-channel incrementality, identity resolution, B2B buying-group signal loss, and ad supply integrity, where fraud and real performance both look like numbers going up.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the people who hold the answer gain nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. The blockers are money and politics, inside the company as much as outside, so the models try to make honesty or cooperation pay rather than write another rule.
themes.evidence: On agentic traffic the models offer fast lanes and better prices to agents that declare themselves because spoofing currently pays, on journey orchestration they note channel owners are paid on their own numbers, on the semantic context layer they call conflicting definitions a political settlement, and on ad supply integrity they say the parties measuring the traffic often profit from it.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Every model answering safe agent execution puts a proxy or gateway in front of every write with hard spend and audience caps, the consent enforcement answers funnel all data exits through one checkpoint, and the orchestration answers route every channel send through one shared contact log that can say no.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch from outside and estimate whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: On downstream consent and deletion all three models call ad platforms and trained models black boxes where a person's influence cannot be extracted or proven removed, and the same opacity drives the incrementality answers, where platforms control both the treatment and the evidence.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning and context: whether a picture plus a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, whether two teams can both be right about what a word means. No rule set captures that, so the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it.
themes.evidence: On generative content governance the models build an approved-claims library and restrict writing to it because implied meaning cannot be checked automatically, and on the semantic context layer they conclude that competing definitions of customer or revenue are legitimate and must be disclosed rather than collapsed.
